exposure: time until pushing (TUP) after full cervical dilation
cohort: The study included 228 nulliparous women with singleton pregnancy, planned vaginal delivery after 36 completed weeks of gestation, epidural analgesia, and guided active pushing.
finding: Longer time until pushing after full cervical dilation correlated significantly with increased postpartum maternal blood loss, measured by decreased hemoglobin and higher rates of significant hemoglobin decrease.
mod_finding: Longer time until active pushing during planned vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia was significantly correlated with increased maternal blood loss.
